A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OCN/OCNP research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original OCN/OCNP benchmark results, ablations, and runtime and memory measurements, including supplementary experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark, ablation, and scalability results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The batch-based orthogonalization, path-based normalization, polynomial-filter variant, and prediction architecture remain unchanged. The added pair indexing in Equation (7) clarifies notation without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same seven datasets: Cora, Citeseer, Pubmed, ogbl-collab, ogbl-ppa, ogbl-citation2, and ogbl-ddi. Barabási–Albert graphs are introduced for theoretical analysis, not as an evaluated dataset or simulation.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the benchmark, supplementary, backbone, and scalability comparisons. Tables 1 and 8 retain the same methods, including NCN/NCNC, BUDDY, PLNLP, and GIDN in their respective comparisons.

E3.justification: The metrics, dataset splits, target-link removal, model configurations, and optimization settings remain unchanged in Appendices F–H and Tables 3–5. No new empirical protocol accompanies the theoretical extension.

E4.justification: The component, backbone, higher-order-neighbor, and shortest-path ablations, along with coefficient and parameter-norm analyses, are retained. v1's Appendix Q ablation discussion moves verbatim into v2's Section 7.2; it is not a new analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over 10 runs with different random seeds and standard deviations. The new checklist reiterates existing uncertainty reporting without adding statistical procedures or runs.

E6.justification: The empirical tables and plotted results are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains ogbl-ppa scores of 69.79±0.85 for OCN and 74.87±0.94 for OCNP; the supplementary results and runtime measurements also match.

T1.justification: v2 adds Barabási–Albert graph and link-score definitions, degree and path-probability derivations, and normalized versus unnormalized bounds in Propositions 5.5–5.6 and Appendix Q. This substantially extends the formal analysis beyond the retained latent-space theory, including a new Lambert W derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: addressing redundancy and over-smoothing through OCN/OCNP, theoretical support, and benchmark improvements. The claimed average 7.7% improvement is unchanged.

C2.justification: The new Appendix Q explicitly notes that the original random-graph analysis may not capture real-network structure. Section 5.1 interprets the added Barabási–Albert bounds as extending normalization's benefits to a more realistic model. Existing ablation interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit code-repository link in the abstract and states in the checklist that source code accompanies the submission. Hardware, hyperparameters, algorithms, and training details are unchanged. The PDFs establish the access statements, not the repository's contents.

R1.justification: v2 adds Albert and Barabási's 2002 Statistical Mechanics of Complex Networks reference to support the theoretical extension. The remaining bibliography and positioning relative to existing link-prediction methods are retained.

P1.justification: Most prose and section organization remain unchanged. Local revisions move the detailed ablation discussion into Section 7.2, add the theoretical appendix and checklist, update affiliations, and replace template acknowledgments with an actual funding statement.

P2.justification: v1's two-panel Figure 2 becomes separate Figures 2 and 3 with expanded captions and text wrapping. Other figures are relocated or resized, and hyperlinks gain color. The underlying plots and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 improves code discoverability and presentation, but its principal scientific addition has unresolved consistency problems. Section 5.1 states probability guarantees of 1−δ whereas Appendix Q states δ; Equation (102) supplies an upper probability bound where Equation (105) requires a lower bound. These issues undermine confidence in the added theoretical support. With unchanged empirical evidence and limited documentation benefits, a reliable net quality direction cannot be established.
